findings.summary: Telling the producer to mark an uncheckable criterion unmet triggers the self-check send-back. A job with such a criterion uses up its send-back rounds before it fails, instead of failing at once.

summary: The change passes. The reader brief and the producer brief now both state, from one shared constant, that every acceptance criterion must be checkable from the snapshot, the diff or the commands the verifier runs, never from the producer's report or change description. A new test renders each brief and checks for the rule as literal text. I ran both tests and the full athena-context suite (124 of 124 passed); Athena's record shows the producer-brief test failing with the fix reverted. Section 5 of docs/design/structure-pass.md now puts the caller check and its other proofs in the committed tests or in commands the verifier reruns, and no item in the section rests on the report. The test the doc names (a_landing_touching_a_file_under_gh_selects_d87_and_d88) exists. Only the three expected files changed, the existing brief wording is untouched, no prompt file changed, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. I found three minor issues, none blocking: the doc overstates that tests "run" every old-path hit, the test-name proof in item 2 is weak for the G8 and R9 moves, and a criterion marked unmet as uncheckable uses up send-back rounds before the job fails.
